request.spec:
A DRAFT claim can be deleted (a button on the claim; any other status, or a claim in a closed
period, is refused with an error on the claim): its status becomes DELETED, it counts nowhere (not
in any total, not in the status counts of the header or the summary), it cannot be edited, opened
or voided, its log gains a DELETED line, and CLAIM_DELETED is written naming the claim. On the same
sheet-today it was deleted, a restore button makes it a DRAFT again (CLAIM_RESTORED, a DRAFT line in
the log); on a later day the restore is refused.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A DRAFT claim can be deleted (a button on the claim; any other status, or a claim in a closed
period, is refused with an error on the claim): its status becomes DELETED, it counts nowhere (not
in any total, not in the status counts of the header or the summary), it cannot be edited, opened
or voided, its log gains a DELETED line, and CLAIM_DELETED is written naming the claim. On the same
sheet-today it was deleted, a restore button makes it a DRAFT again (CLAIM_RESTORED, a DRAFT line in
the log); on a later day the restore is refused.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
DRAFT claims can now be deleted and restored. `bin/e2e` passes: the new delete/restore test and the three other scenarios in the spec all pass.

**Server**
- I added `delete` and `restore` as two more claim actions on the existing status-change endpoint (`{action}.POST.yml`), so they go through the same checks as open and void: archived sheet, viewer role, closed period, writing the log line and the audit record.
- **Delete** only works on a DRAFT and makes it DELETED. **Restore** only works on a DELETED claim and makes it a DRAFT again. Restore is refused unless the sheet's today matches the date of the claim's latest DELETED log line, so a later day is refused.
- The audit lines are `CLAIM_DELETED …` and `CLAIM_RESTORED …`, with the person, amount and date of the claim.
- DELETED is a new status in `ClaimStatus.java`. It needed no other changes to stay out of everything:
  - It counts in no total, because totals only include OPEN, PENDING and SETTLED.
  - It can't be edited, opened or voided, because each of those requires another status.
  - It can't be moved to another person, for the same reason.
- I also stopped a deleted claim from being given a proof, in `Claim.java`.
- The status is stored as text in the existing column, so no database migration was needed.

**Front end**
- Each claim has new Delete and Restore buttons (`claim-delete` / `claim-restore`). A refusal shows in the claim's existing `claim-error`.
- I added DELETED to the claim status type. The header and summary count only the five existing statuses, so deleted claims don't appear in either.

One thing to be aware of: in the test, a DRAFT dated 2026-02-05 inside the closed period P1 can still be deleted. That's because this app decides "in a closed period" by a claim's due-by date, not its claim date, and that claim's due-by falls after P1. Every other claim action already works this way, and the test expects it.
